sentences.text: . Ranglal, father of the revisionist is deponent in present revision.
The notice issued to opposite party no. 2 and informant's guardian/father of the victim through C.J.M. concerned, but he has not appear to contest the present revision on her behalf.

Heard learned counsel for the revisionist as well as learned AGA for the State and perused the impugned orders along with entire material on record which appears to be complete and enough sufficient to decide this revision.

The factual matrix of the case in brief are that the informant lodged the first information report at P.S. Jhangaha, District Gorakhpur on 29.06.2023 at 19:55 p.m. stating that his daughter studies in Class I0th and she is aged about 16 years.

Co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar who is neighbor seduced and abducted his grand daughter and took her to the shop of revisionist-accused Dheeraj Nishad and committed filthy act with her in a room situated in back portion of the shop.
When he proceeded in search of his grand daughter, she was produced at concerned police station.
His grand daughter told him the present revisionist and co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar committed bad act with her.
The first information report was lodged under sections 363, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act.
The victim in her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C. stated that she is aged about 16 years and she was love in affair with co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar.
Co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar met her prior to the incident and they had established physical relationship also.
The revisionist Dheeraj Nishad made a video at his shop while they were engaging in sexual relationship with her and threatened her to viral the video.

The victim refused to her enteral examination when she was produced before the Medical Officer at District Women Hospital, Gorakhpur and according to the doctor she stated that she was not seduced on 24.06.2023 but co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar established physical relationship with her in past.
The victim in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar established sexual relationship with her in May, 2023.

She was contacted with the co-accused Neeraj Rajbhar for last two years prior to the incident dated 24.06.2023 and also on that date he lept her in the shop of revisionist-accused Dheeraj Nishad after making physical relationship with her.

sentences.text: The revisionist-accused Dheeraj Nishad was declared juvenile in context of law by order dated 08.11.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Gorakhpur.
He is not having any prior criminal antecedents.

The District Probation Officer, Gorakhpur in report dated 10.11.2023 he has not recorded any adverse fact with regard to the family of the revisionist and only stated therein that the control of the parents is lacking to the juvenile.
He is also in custody of Government Observation Home and no adverse report has been received with regard to his conduct and behavior during his confinement in Government Observation Home.

Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice Board,
Gorakhpur has rejected the prayer for bail raised by the revisionist in mechanical manner without considering the purporte and scope of Section 12 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 in the impugned order dated 25.11.2023 and the same has been affirmed by the Children Board in appellate order dated 19.12.2023 without considering the grounds taken in appeal in proper manner.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further submitted that the gravity of the offence is not a ground for rejection of bail and that too when the case of enlargement of applicant on bail stands on better footing to that of co-accused on merits of the case also.

Section 12 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 provides as under:
" 12. (1) When any person, who is apparently a child and is alleged to have committed a bailable or non-bailable offence, is apprehended or detained by the police or appears or brought before a Board, such person shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 or in any other law for the time being in force, be released on bail with or without surety or placed under the supervision of a probation officer or under the care of any fit person:
Provided that such person shall not be so released if there appears reasonable grounds for believing that the release is likely to bring that person into association with any known criminal or expose the said person to moral, physical or psychological danger or the person's release would defeat the ends of justice, and the Board shall record the reasons for denying the bail and circumstances that led to such a decision.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: ( 2 ) When such person having been apprehended is not released on bail under subsection (1) by the officer-in-charge of the police station, such officer shall cause the person to be kept only in an observation home in such manner as may be prescribed until the person can be brought before a Board.

(3) When such person is not released on bail under sub-section (1) by the Board, it shall make an order sending him to an observation home or a place of safety, as the case may be, for such period during the pendency of the inquiry regarding the person,

sentences.text: (4 ) When a child in conflict with law is unable to fulfil the conditions of bail order within seven days of the bail order, such child shall be produced before the Board for modification of the conditions of bail."

On perusal of aforesaid statutory provision it is manifest that bail to juvenile justice of law can only be denied, if 3 conditions fulfilled:
(i). If there appears reasonable grounds for believing that the release is likely to bring that person into association with any known criminal (ii). Or expose the said person to moral, physical or psychological danger.
(iii). Or the person's release would defeat the ends of justice.
It is also provided under Section 12 that the Board shall record the reasons for denying the bail and circumstances that led to such a decision.

Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the allegations against the revisionist are of serious in nature but not in disputed the legal position that bail can only be denied on fulfillment of any of the grounds mentioned under Section 12 (i) of the Act.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and material on record there is nothing to suggest that the release of the revisionist is likely to bring him into association with any criminal or expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger or that his release would defeat the ends of the justice.
In these circumstances, the Board was not quite justified in rejecting the bail application of the revisionist.

Learned Children Court was fell in error while dismissing the appeal preferred by the revisionist under Section 101 of the Act and affirming the finding of order of Juvenile Justice Board while dismissing the bail application of the revisionist.
Accordingly, the revision is hereby allowed.
The impugned order dated 25.11.2023 passed by the Juvenile justice Board by learned Children Court/POCSO Court, Gorakhpur are hereby set-aside.

The revisionist-Dheeraj Nishad S/o Shri Ranglal, resident of Village-Rasulpur No. 2 Tola Luxmipur,
P.S. Jhangaha, District Gorakhpur involved in Case Crime No. 316 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jhangaha, District Gorakhpur be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond through his legal guardian/father and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Board concerned.
